findings.title: The step is launch bound
findings.evidence: the device is busy 7% of the step (744 of 10967 ms) over 32959 launches and 657072 operators per step, 327 us of host time per launch
findings.lever: graph replay is already running for some steps; compare replayed and eager step times above

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: conv output_blocks.in_layers (up)
findings.evidence: 722.5 ms per step against an ideal 20.7 ms (3% efficient, compute-bound), 9 layers; all rated pieces together leave 13107 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: conv output_blocks.skip_connection (up)
findings.evidence: 484.2 ms per step against an ideal 2.5 ms (1% efficient, compute-bound), 9 layers; all rated pieces together leave 13107 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn1 (up)
findings.evidence: 458.0 ms per step against an ideal 9.8 ms (2% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 13107 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn2 (up)
findings.evidence: 438.9 ms per step against an ideal 9.8 ms (2% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 13107 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear ff.net (up)
findings.evidence: 394.5 ms per step against an ideal 9.1 ms (2% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 13107 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Dtype and copy kernels take a large share
findings.evidence: 21% of device time is casts and copies
findings.lever: find the modules issuing `.to(dtype)` round trips (autocast boundaries, adapter branches) and keep one dtype through them

findings.title: Many small memory-bound kernels
findings.evidence: 39% of device time (20397 calls per step) is elementwise, normalisation, copy, memory and reduction work
findings.lever: fusion (fewer, larger kernels): norm + modulation, activation + multiply, cast + matmul input; half the time is the most a fusion usually recovers

findings.title: The int8 path's own kernels are a large share
findings.evidence: rotate, quantize and dequantize kernels are 19% of device time against 194 ms of matmuls
findings.lever: int8_grad=int8 (no weight dequantize in backward), or a fused rotate+quantize in the kernels project; native weights if memory allows
